chapter: Parisian Room and Bourbon Street clubs
title: Comparing Manny's and El Morocco
summary: El Morocco was a small typical Bourbon Street club; Manny's was larger, informal with dancing, and the band played a wider repertoire there.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Do you remember uh enough to compare the El Morocco or El Morocco and Manny's?

Uh I remember how do you mean the band or? The band and the places the effect the place out on the band. Well El Morocco was relatively small compared to Manny's. Uh huh. And El Morocco was to me a fairly typical Bourbon Street nightclub.
Uh. Uh. Manny's they played Friday and Saturday nights as a rule. Uh huh. Uh to a fairly large, it was a fairly large room.

And there were more people who were interested in listening to the music. When I say more, it wasn't a lot more but it was more. Uh huh. And more people who knew what they were coming to listen to than at the El Morocco. Uh huh. Uh huh. Uh the band, the band actually was a lot more casual and informal at Manny's. Uh huh. And the music seemed more relaxed. I know I enjoyed Manny's more. I think partly because people were dancing. And they, I don't think they were dancing at the El Morocco. Basically, at the El Morocco you sat at a bar, at the bar. Uh huh. Or at some tables. And there was no dance floor. And the band in effect played a concert. And uh, it was, it was frequently good but it wasn't the same and I didn't enjoy it as much as I did at Manny's. Also at the El Morocco they hustled you more for drinks.
Uh huh. Do you remember that there was any difference in the selections that the band played? Between the two places?
Uh huh. It seems to me that the selection narrowed at El Morocco. Uh huh.
